title: Tim Curry, star of The Rocky Horror Picture Show dies at 80
seoTitle: Tim Curry, star of The Rocky Horror Picture Show dies at.
subtitle: The British actor left his mark on film and theater with iconic roles such as Dr. Frank‑N‑Furter and the clown Pennywise
excerpt: Actor Tim Curry died at 80 at his Los Angeles home. He was known for iconic roles like Dr. Frank‑N‑Furter and the clown Pennywise.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The renowned British actor Tim Curry died at 80 at his home in Los Angeles, as announced by his longtime manager and friend Marcia Hurwitz. The artist, who had been dealing with serious health issues and used a wheelchair after suffering a stroke in 2012, marked generations with his versatility in film, television, and theater.

The success of The Rocky Horror Picture Show

Tim Curry began his career on stage in the original production of *Hair* and helped develop the mad scientist Dr. Frank‑N‑Furter for *The Rocky Horror Show* at the Royal Court Theatre in London. The actor took the role to the London and Broadway stages, and starred in the 1975 film adaptation alongside Susan Sarandon and Barry Bostwick. The movie became a cult classic shown at midnight screenings, where audiences would dress up and interact with the projection.

Memorable characters in film and television

Across five decades of work, Curry built a vast gallery of memorable characters, often portraying villains and eccentric figures. In 1990, he played the terrifying clown Pennywise in the television adaptation of *It*, based on Stephen King’s novel. He also appeared in productions such as *Annie*, *Home Alone 2: Lost in New York*, *Clue*, *The Hunt for Red October* and *The Three Musketeers*.

Award nominations and stage work

Recognized in the artistic community, the actor received three Tony Award nominations throughout his theater career. The first came for his performance as Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart in the play *Amadeus* in 1981, followed by nominations in 1993 for the musical *My Favorite Year* and in 2005 for his role as King Arthur in the musical *Monty Python's Spamalot*. Curry also earned Emmy nominations and won a Daytime Emmy in 1990 for his voice work as Captain Hook.

Voice‑over work and recent projects

Beyond his live‑action roles, Curry lent his voice to several successful animated characters, such as Hexxus in *FernGully: The Last Rainforest* and Nigel Thornberry in *The Wild Thornberrys*. In recent years, despite the limitations caused by his health problems, he continued voice acting—appearing in *Star Wars: The Clone Wars* as Chancellor Palpatine/Darth Sidious—and made an appearance in the horror film *Stream*, released in August 2024.

With information from TMZ, The Hollywood Reporter.
